refuted.why: FALSE. I fetched the feed: 20 entries, but the window runs from 2026-08-11T13:59:21Z to 2026-09-16T13:59:28Z, and the target article IS in it. Its entry reads <updated>2026-08-18T15:59:46.948Z</updated> with <category term="UPDATE"/> and the exact article URL. So an official Apple feed date for the Newsroom item does exist; the researcher wrongly declared it unavailable and relied on page JSON-LD instead. It also conflicts with the page's JSON-LD dateModified of 2026-08-27, which the writer needs to know.

refuted.fact: verified_fact 43, clause: "Unlike the Japan/Brazil attachment, the EU attachment adds NO separate payment-processing fee on top of the 20%."
refuted.why: Mis-mapped to the wrong row. In Attachment 12 (Additional Terms for iOS Apps in Japan, Brazil) the extra "five percent (5%) fee for the App Store's payment processing and related commerce services" attaches to Section 3.5(C), which is Apple's OWN in-app purchase system at twenty-one percent (21%) - not to Alternative Payment Processing, which is Section 3.5(B) and also 21%. There is therefore no "on top of the 20%" equivalent being compared. It is also the researcher's own cross-attachment analysis, not a statement either document makes, so it should not sit in verified_facts at all. The EU Attachment 14 Section 3.5 does indeed contain no extra processing fee - that part is correct - but the comparison as written is wrong.

additional_findings: BETTER FIRST-PARTY DATE ANCHOR the researcher declared unavailable: the Apple Newsroom Atom feed carries this article with <updated>2026-08-18T15:59:46.948Z</updated> and <category term="UPDATE"/>. It CONFLICTS with the page's own JSON-LD dateModified of 2026-08-27, so "the text read today is the 27 August revision" must be written as what the page's JSON-LD says, not as established revision history.

MATERIAL DIVERGENCE BETWEEN TWO APPLE PAGES ON CHILD SAFETY, present only in corrections_to_candidate_list and never as a source-attached verified_fact. Newsroom says "For users under 18 years old ... must include a parental gate" and "Apps in the Kids category ... will not include links to websites". BOTH support pages instead say: Kids category apps "must place purchase flows that use an alternative payment processor behind a parental gate, AND cannot provide an out-of-app offer to purchase on a website"; "For users under 13 years old, alternative payment purchases must be behind a parental gate, and out-of-app offers are not permitted"; "For users 13 years old to 17 years old, both alternative payment processing within the app and out-of-app purchase offers must be behind a parental gate." Writing only the Newsroom "under 18" framing understates the under-13 rule. The support pages also give the worked example Apple's Newsroom omits: "in some storefronts the protections apply to users under 16 (instead of under 13) and 16 to 17 (instead of 13 to 17)."

RATE-TABLE GAP: facts 11 and 25 omit that the 10% alternative-payment-processing tier ALSO covers auto-renewable subscriptions after their first year. The Newsroom does not say this; developer.apple.com/support/apps-in-the-eu/ does, verbatim: "10% - Sales processed via alternative payment processing within the app from participants in the App Store Small Business Program, Mini Apps Partner Program, or Video Partner Program, and sales of auto-renewable subscriptions after their first year." This matters because BRIEF.md requires a table.

The two Apple pages word the 15% store-services row differently: apps-in-the-eu says "15% - Out-of-app offers, excluding transactions from program participants or auto-renewable subscriptions after their first year"; payment-options says only "15% - Out-of-app offers." Cite whichever page the table is built from.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERION DIVERGENCE not flagged: Newsroom says "Are a government entity, educational institution, or nonprofit." Both support pages say "Are a government entity, educational institution, or nonprofit APPROVED FOR A FEE WAIVER." Fact 18 quotes Newsroom accurately, but the difference should be recorded.

LIVE-DOCUMENT CAVEAT MISSED, which BRIEF.md warns about explicitly: the Apple Developer Program License Agreement page returns Last-Modified Thu, 10 Sep 2026 17:29:10 GMT - the binding text was revised AFTER the 18 August announcement. Any Attachment 14 quotation must be dated "as read on 2026-09-16", not treated as the as-published 18 August text.

CTC SCOPE UNDER-RECORDED: apps-in-the-eu lists three transaction categories the 5% Core Technology Commission covers, including sales "required to access or download alternative app marketplaces ... including paid subscriptions to access or download app content or catalogs of apps" and link-out sales "made within 7 days of the link tap". Facts 13 and 25 carry only the one-line Newsroom version.

Not captured, both first-party: apps in the EU subject to "Guideline 3.1.3(b) Multiplatform Services" must offer Apple In-App Purchase and/or alternative in-app payment processing (payment-options page); and reader apps in the EU may promote out-of-app offers without an actionable link (apps-in-the-eu page).

Apple's licence agreement quantifies the Dun & Bradstreet bar the Newsroom leaves vague - a "Global Business Ranking" score qualifying for the "Low Risk" or "Below Average Risk" categories defined by D&B. I confirmed the researcher's not_said note that this detail exists only in the licence agreement, not in the announcement.

Minor refinement to sourcing_notes: ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner is partly reachable after all - /api/rss?language=en returns valid RSS (HTTP 200, 10 items, newest 2026-09-16). But size= and text= params are ignored and it is a 10-item rolling window, so it cannot reach August. The researcher's conclusion (attribute nothing to the Commission) still stands, just for a different reason.
NO DISQUALIFYING SOURCING FOUND. Every fact traces to an Apple first-party page; no news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet appears anywhere in the record.

Announcement 2026-08-18 and effective 2026-10-01 are kept separate throughout; fact 9 correctly reproduces the Newsroom's year-less "October 1" without inventing a year; event_date and slug date are right; Apple Developer RSS pubDate "Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:00:38 PDT" confirmed by me.
